---
title: "Getting started"
description: "Fit transitions, project a cohort and calculate outcomes from synthetic single-episode histories."
---

This example uses one synthetic history per patient. It fits transitions,
projects a cohort and calculates economic outcomes without a database.

## Install the package

From a checkout of the
[repository](https://github.com/HealthInformaticsUT/TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis),
set R's working directory to the package folder and install its `Imports`
dependencies from `DESCRIPTION`. Then install the checkout:

```r
install.packages(".", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

Restart R if an older TMA build was loaded. `CDMConnector` is needed for
database-backed cost extraction; Cohort2Trajectory is needed for examples that
create histories through C2T.

## Run the synthetic example

```{r quickstart, results='hide', message=FALSE}
library(TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis)
source(system.file("examples", "quickstart.R", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis"),
       local = TRUE)
```

The script creates `trajectories`, `histories`, `transitions`, `projection`,
`cost_records` and `costs`. Each patient has one history on a seven-day grid,
using `Stable`, `Complication` and absorbing `Dead` states. All amounts and
probabilities are illustrative.

Inspect the fitted probabilities:

```{r probabilities}
transitionMatrix(transitions)
```

`transitions$estimates` also contains observed counts and denominators. The
projection starts with 100 stable patients and takes four adjacent-cycle steps.
Here are its first and last snapshots:

```{r occupancy}
subset(projection$occupancy, cycle %in% c(0, 4))
```

Expected counts may be fractional. The cost estimates come from the separate
synthetic records; they do not automatically charge the projection:

```{r recorded-costs}
costs$estimates[c("cost_state", "observed_days", "total_cost", "mean_cost_per_day")]
```

## Calculate completed-interval outcomes

Continue in the same R session:

```{r outcomes}
rewards <- createRewardModel(
  stateCosts = c(Stable = 100, Complication = 200, Dead = 0),
  aliveStates = c("Stable", "Complication"),
  utilities = c(Stable = 0.8, Complication = 0.6, Dead = 0),
  currency = "EUR", priceYear = 2026
)
outcomes <- summariseOutcomes(projection, rewards)
outcomeTotals(outcomes)
outcomeTotals(outcomes, perPatient = TRUE)
```

These supplied state costs are amounts per seven-day interval. Utilities and
costs are example assumptions. The four completed intervals span 28 days; the
last endpoint adds no extra interval. Discount rates default to zero.

For interventions and comparisons, continue with
[costs and economic outcomes](costs-and-economic-outcomes.html) or the
[ordered-stage example](https://github.com/HealthInformaticsUT/TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis/blob/main/inst/examples/ordered-stage-economics.R).

## Use your own histories

A local table needs `subject_id`, `state_label`, `state_start_date` and
`state_end_date`. Dates include both endpoints. Supply your clinical definitions:

```r
# rows contains your single-episode histories.
histories <- prepareTrajectories(
  rows, cycleLength = 7,
  states = c("Stable", "Complication", "Dead"), absorbingStates = "Dead"
)
transitions <- estimateTransitions(histories)
```

C2T First-mode output with a `trajectory_definition` attribute supplies omitted
cycle length, state order and absorbing states. RDS preserves that attribute;
CSV does not. C2T All-mode repeated-episode output is not currently supported.
Removing episode fields or attributes does not make those histories suitable
for TMA. See [preparing histories](preparing-histories.html).

Use your own state labels and absorbing-state definitions. Preparation does not
validate C2T allowed-transition rules. Inspect support before projection:
unestimated probability rows remain `NA` and cause an error when needed.

Browse the [examples](examples.html) for complete analyses, or open the installed
vignette with `vignette("trajectory-analysis", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis")`
when the package was installed with vignettes built.
